entities.summary: Samson Slaying a Philistine is a marble sculpture created around 1562 by Giambologna, one of the most significant artists of the late Renaissance. Originally commissioned by Francesco de' Medici for a fountain in Florence, this sculpture was later gifted to Spain's Duke of Lerma and displayed in the gardens of the Palacio de la Ribera, Valladolid. The work marked a significant milestone in Giambologna's career, embodying both artistic mastery and Medici influence, symbolizing their political power through a dramatic biblical scene.
